reason: I attacked this one expecting to win and lost. The note makes an unusual claim, that the wording is exact including on the other hand without commas, and my memory of the letter had the commas in, as nearly every modern reprint does: You, on the other hand, have labored in a private way. So I fetched the DocSouth transcription of the 1869 Auburn printing, stripped the markup and read the letter from salutation to signature. The 1869 text reads Most that I have done and suffered in the service of our cause has been in public, and I have received much encouragement at every step of the way. You on the other hand have labored in a private way. No commas. The note is right and the modern reprints are the ones that drift. The proposal matches the 1869 setting word for word and comma for comma. The page correction holds too. DocSouth keeps the page break markers, and Page 7 opens at kind lady, and that the same is so soon to be published, exactly as the locator says, with Page 8 not arriving until Much that you have done would seem improbable. Both quoted sentences fall between those markers, so p. 7 is correct and the letter does begin at the foot of page 6. The heading is ROCHESTER, August 29, 1868, signed FREDERICK DOUGLASS, under the section head Letter from Frederick Douglass, so the date and the addressee are right. Attribution: Douglass’s own letter, printed in Bradford’s book, and the source line says exactly that rather than crediting Bradford with the words; nothing on the misattribution list touches it. Scope: 1869, a letter in a named book, no scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory. Publishable: the hard matter in that letter, the trembling and foot-sore and the house of bondage and John Brown, all falls outside the cut; what is quoted is two clean sentences about public and private labour and needs no warning. Tag: Correspondence, the form of the work. The structure, a letter printed inside an edited volume, matches the precedent already in the carry for Thoreau’s Familiar Letters and Alcott’s Life, Letters, and Journals. Source line: 133 characters, leads with the name, no dash, no straight quote, ends in a full stop. Cap: shipped.js gives frederick douglass at 0 of 3, not banned, nothing shipped and no near opening. Theme: public praise set against unseen private work is September’s question put better than almost anything else in the month.
